newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico preliminary May trade surplus $88 mln.
newsitem.headline: Mexico preliminary May trade surplus $88 mln.

text.p: Mexico's preliminary trade balance surplus for May was $88 million compared with a revised $50 million in April, the Finance Ministry said.
The May figure was way below market expectations. A Reuter survey of analysts' forecasts showed an average expectation of $184.72 million.
May exports totalled $8.776 billion, up 8.7 percent from May 1996. Imports totalled $8.688 billion, a rise of 16.1 percent.
The ministry said manufactured goods accounted for 84.8 percent of May's consumer exports, petroleum products 10.5 percent, agro-fishery goods 4.2 percent, and non-petroleum products 0.5 percent.
Consumer goods accounted for 7.7 percent of May imports, capital goods accounted for 13.6 percent, and intermediate goods accounted for 78.7 percent, the ministry said.
The accumulated trade balance to May showed a $1.652 billion surplus.
Within the export sector, manufacturing showed the most dramatic increase over the January to May period, rising 14.6 percent.

Capital goods showed the strongest rise on the import side, climbing 37.0 percent over the five months to May, while imports of consumer goods rose 29.4 percent and intermediate goods rose 16.4 percent.
